pathway.title: Ashland Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The business profile is adequate rather than strong, because earnings depend on two segments and two chemistries in a fragmented field where larger rivals have more resources. Life Sciences and Personal Care earned Adjusted EBITDA margins of 33.33% and 29.03% in Q3 2026 against 14.71% in Specialty Additives and an EBITDA margin of 10.81% in Intermediates, and cellulosics and polyvinylpyrrolidones made up 64% of nine-month sales. No single customer exceeded 10% of sales, which limits customer concentration risk, but the competitive structure limits how far cost increases can be passed on. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 180; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K-27; calculation K-26

- Earnings are eroding even as sales recover, and this is the central weakness. Trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 384 million is 16.34% below fiscal 2024, and over nine months sales rose 1.34% while adjusted EBITDA fell 6.03%, taking the margin from 20.94% to 19.41%. Life Sciences and Personal Care both report unfavorable price and mix, so growth has come from volume and currency, and guidance implies fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 120 million to USD 135 million against USD 119 million a year earlier. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation K-05; calculation K-07; calculation K-06; calculation K-09

- Leverage is moderate and has fallen in each quarter of fiscal 2026, but part of the improvement is cash that will not recur. Net debt to trailing adjusted EBITDA moved from 2.92x at fiscal 2025 year end to 2.43x, the covenant ratio is 2.3x against a 4.0x maximum and coverage is 6.9x against a 3.0x minimum, yet the cash build of USD 225 million includes the USD 103 million refund, and on an analyst adjustment leverage without it would be 2.70x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation K-01; calculation K-02; calculation K-03; calculation K-04; calculation K-15

- Cash conversion has been uneven, and the 2026 recovery owes much to working capital and a refund. Free cash flow was USD 325 million in fiscal 2024 after USD 227 million of working-capital release, USD 36 million in fiscal 2025 after USD 191 million was absorbed, and USD 141 million in nine months 2026 without the refund. Cash used by discontinued operations, which the issuer's measure excludes, turns fiscal 2025 into a USD 4 million shortfall before dividends, and recurring add-backs of USD 75 million make up 19.53% of the earnings base. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 64; calculation K-10; calculation K-12; calculation K-11; calculation K-24

- Liquidity is adequate and the maturity wall is distant, which protects creditors until fiscal 2028, when USD 571 million of euro notes fall due. Liquidity of USD 936 million is made of cash of USD 440 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 496 million that was cut by USD 100 million in May 2026, and USD 177 million of receivables sold under two programs is funding outside the debt figure, with the USD 68 million U.S. program scheduled to end on 2026-09-11. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 151; calculation K-16; calculation K-17; calculation K-18; calculation K-30

- Legacy asbestos and environmental claims are a standing drain on cash and a source of estimate risk. Reserves of USD 676 million are matched by trusts and insurance receivables except for USD 188 million, the environmental range reaches USD 249 million above the reserve, and the fiscal 2026 model update raised asbestos reserves by USD 48 million against a USD 22 million rise in insurance receivables, so the exposure can move against creditors faster than earnings can offset it. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 65; calculation K-21; calculation K-22; calculation K-23

- Financial policy is conservative for now but not committed. Shareholder returns of USD 458 million in fiscal 2024 and USD 176 million in fiscal 2025 exceeded free cash flow, only dividends of USD 57 million were paid in nine months 2026, and a repurchase authorization remains open, while two agency downgrades in fiscal 2026 point to weaker agency views even though both outlooks are stable. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation K-25; calculation K-35

- The primary downside path is cost inflation that pricing does not offset in the two core chemistries, which would pull adjusted EBITDA down while legacy and dividend cash needs stay fixed. A USD 50 million fall in adjusted EBITDA would lift net leverage to 2.80x, adjusted EBITDA near USD 311 million would put it at 3.00x, and either would arrive ahead of the fiscal 2028 refinancing. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation K-20; calculation K-19

cells.text: A global additives and specialty ingredients company serving pharmaceutical, personal care, coatings, construction, energy and food markets, with about 2,900 employees and customers in more than 100 countries
Many end markets cushion a single-market downturn, but the range rests on cellulose and vinyl pyrrolidone chemistry
Four reportable segments; in nine months 2026 Life Sciences was 36%, Personal Care 31%, Specialty Additives 27% and Intermediates 6% of sales (35%, 31%, 28%, 6% a year earlier)

Pharmaceutical and personal-care ingredients carry the margin; Specialty Additives serves over 30 industries at a lower margin, and Intermediates is a small butanediol business that also supplies the other segments as a raw material
Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin: Life Sciences 33.3%, Personal Care 29.0%, Specialty Additives 14.7%; Intermediates EBITDA margin 10.8%
Group margin depends on two segments; the weakest two earn too little to offset a shock to them
Cellulosics 40% and polyvinylpyrrolidones 24% of nine-month 2026 sales, 64% together
Two chemistries drive about two-thirds of sales, so raw-material cost and supply shocks (cotton linters, wood pulp, hydrocarbon derivatives) reach most of the group

Customers include pharmaceutical and food manufacturers, formulators at large branded consumer-products companies and smaller independents, and paint, electronics and automotive manufacturers; no single customer represented more than 10% of sales in fiscal 2023, 2024 or 2025
Single-customer risk is limited, though contract terms and pricing pass-through are not disclosed
73% of nine-month 2026 sales outside North America: Europe 36%, Asia Pacific 27%, Latin America and other 10%, North America 27%
Earnings and the euro notes are exposed to the euro and to tariff and trade-policy changes

Life Sciences 11 manufacturing and lab facilities in nine countries, Personal Care 9 in ten, Specialty Additives 8 in eight, and an Intermediates plant in Lima, Ohio; a multi-year optimization targets USD 50 million to USD 55 million of pre-tax savings, USD 10 million realized in nine months
A network being restructured carries restructuring cash costs and accelerated depreciation that the issuer adds back to Adjusted EBITDA
Demand is stronger in warmer months; energy and raw-material costs were stable in fiscal 2023 to 2025 but are described as elevated in 2026, with pricing actions expected to offset them
Pass-through of costs is the main margin lever and lags in a fast cost move

Fiscal 2026 guidance: sales USD 1,835 million to USD 1,870 million, Adjusted EBITDA USD 385 million to USD 400 million, Ongoing Free Cash Flow conversion above 50% of Adjusted EBITDA with capital expenditure about USD 90 million
Management Language: flat earnings on stable sales; implied fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA is USD 120 million to USD 135 million

runs.text: The first strength is high-margin, defensible earnings in two segments. Life Sciences and Personal Care earned Adjusted EBITDA margins of 33.33% and 29.03% in Q3 2026 and carry most of the group's profit, which means the earnings base is protected by formulation know-how and a broad end-market reach, and creditors can expect the core to hold margin better than Specialty Additives at 14.71%. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation K-27

The second strength is liquidity and a long runway. Liquidity of USD 936 million and no maturity larger than USD 4 million before the USD 571 million euro notes in fiscal 2028 give the issuer about two years to restore earnings, and the 1.40x cover of the fiscal 2028 and 2029 maturities means refinancing is a market-access question and not a funding gap. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation K-16; calculation K-17

The third strength is flexible spending. Capital expenditure fell 42.35% over two years and is guided to about USD 90 million, repurchases have stopped, and optimization savings are still being realized, so cash can be preserved quickly if earnings weaken. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation K-13; calculation K-28

The first weakness is eroding earnings against rising sales. Trailing adjusted EBITDA is 16.34% below fiscal 2024 and price and mix are unfavorable in the two best segments, so leverage that looks moderate rests on a falling denominator, and any further decline raises leverage and rating pressure directly. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 57; calculation K-05; calculation K-07

The second weakness is concentration in two chemistries exposed to agricultural and hydrocarbon inputs. Cellulosics and polyvinylpyrrolidones make up 64% of sales, and the competitive structure delays cost pass-through, so a cost shock reaches most of the group at once. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation K-26

The third weakness is legacy liabilities and uneven cash conversion. Reserves of USD 676 million leave USD 188 million beyond insurance and trust assets, and free cash flow after discontinued operations was a USD 4 million shortfall in fiscal 2025, so the cash that supports deleveraging is not dependable year to year. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K-21; calculation K-11

The fourth weakness is a weakened rating position and a smaller revolver. Both agencies downgraded Ashland in fiscal 2026 and the committed revolver is USD 100 million smaller at a higher initial margin, which raises the cost and reduces the margin for error in the fiscal 2028 refinancing. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 66; calculation K-18; calculation K-35

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The only debt financing transaction in the period is the Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement of 2026-05-28, which replaced the USD 600 million 2022 revolver with a USD 500 million five-year unsecured revolver for Ashland and its Swiss subsidiary, with a USD 125 million letter of credit sublimit. It prices at 137.5 bp over Term SOFR or EURIBOR to begin with, moving between 125 bp and 175 bp with net leverage, against an initial 125 bp before, and carries an unused fee of 17.5 bp rising to a range of 12.5 bp to 27.5 bp; Ashland paid USD 2 million of issuance costs and keeps financial covenants of a maximum 4.0x net leverage and a minimum 3.0x interest coverage. Committed liquidity is USD 100 million lower, the facility is unsecured, and the obligations of the Swiss borrower are guaranteed by Ashland. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 150; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation C-14

No new notes were issued in fiscal 2025 or the first nine months of 2026: the note stack is the 2028 euro notes, the 2031 notes, the 2043 notes and the 2029 junior subordinated notes in both annual and quarterly debt tables, and the changes in carrying value are currency and accretion. Carrying debt rose by USD 35 million in fiscal 2025 and fell by USD 10 million in the nine months, so the transactions of the period did not add leverage. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 149; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C-19

Two disposals shaped the period. The Nutraceuticals business was sold to Turnspire Capital Partners on 2024-08-30 for USD 26 million net, with a USD 99 million impairment, and the Avoca business was sold to Mane SA on 2025-03-31 for USD 16 million net, with a USD 183 million impairment and a USD 8 million gain; both were non-cash charges against small proceeds, and the Nutraceuticals capital loss produced the USD 103 million tax refund received in the nine months to 2026-06-30. The sales removed lower-return businesses and some earnings: they are part of the reduction in sales and Adjusted EBITDA described above and are not debt-reducing events. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 139; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 138; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 64–65; calculation C-20

The U.S. receivables sale program was amended on 2024-09-13 to lower the buyer limit and extend the scheduled termination to 2026-09-11; the quarterly reports to 2026-06-30 do not restate that date, so whether it was extended or ended is not established. USD 177 million of receivables sold were outstanding under the two programs at 2026-06-30. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 151; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C-22

fields.value: Cash flow in 2026 is stronger than earnings suggest, and part of it will not repeat. fields.value: Business and governance facts for Ashland Inc. (issuer ash-1674862), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the company, its transactions, ownership and control, operating model, governance and capital-allocation behaviour from the five supplied SEC filings, with no sponsor behind the issuer identified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ashland is widely held and no sponsor is identified, so creditor protection rests on its own cash-funded financial policy, and governance risk is medium rather than low because the filings leave control, related-party and policy questions open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a specialty-ingredients portfolio whose earnings rest on two product families and two high-margin segments, and its earnings base has shrunk after disposals, with sales of USD 1,824 million in fiscal 2025 against USD 2,191 million in fiscal 2023. Management guides to full-year Adjusted EBITDA of USD 385 million to USD 400 million, at or below the USD 401 million of fiscal 2025, and the legacy asbestos and environmental claims remain the largest balance-sheet claim outside debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified, which removes the extraction and support questions a sponsor-owned issuer raises but leaves discipline to the board and to public shareholders. The company is listed, has a widely spread share register and a combined chair and chief executive, and expects quarterly dividends comparable to past ones to continue, at the board's discretion; the proxy statement that would show holders and related-party dealings is not supplied, so the control and related-party picture is incomplete rather than clean.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings rest on two product families and on the two segments that earn the most. Cellulosics and polyvinylpyrrolidones were 64% of nine-month sales, and Life Sciences and Personal Care earned Adjusted EBITDA margins of 33.3% and 29.0% in Q3 2026 against 14.7% for Specialty Additives and 10.8% for Intermediates. A raw-material or supply shock to cellulose or vinyl pyrrolidone chemistry would therefore hit most of the group at once, and the weaker segments give little offset.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Portfolio pruning has already cut the earnings base, and the drag is mostly behind. Sales fell 16.75% and Adjusted EBITDA 12.64% between fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2025 after the Nutraceuticals and Avoca sales and the cellulose product-line actions, which cut fiscal 2025 sales by about USD 208 million and Adjusted EBITDA by USD 45 million; in the nine months to 2026-06-30 the same actions cost only USD 11 million of sales and USD 1 million of Adjusted EBITDA. A smaller business carries the same debt, so scale is lower while the obligations are not.

fields.value: - Management's outlook is flat earnings, and the nine months support it only if the fourth quarter holds. Reaffirmed guidance of USD 385 million to USD 400 million of Adjusted EBITDA implies USD 120 million to USD 135 million in the fourth quarter against USD 119 million a year earlier, and USD 470 million to USD 505 million of sales against USD 477 million. Sales are rising and Adjusted EBITDA is falling, so delivery depends on pricing actions offsetting elevated raw-material and freight costs, which is management's statement and not yet shown in results. Management also lowered its adjusted earnings-per-share growth outlook, citing a higher tax rate.

fields.value: - Legacy liabilities are the largest claim outside debt, and trusts and insurance cover only part of them. Combined asbestos and environmental reserves of USD 676 million compare with noncurrent employee benefit obligations of USD 88 million and operating lease obligations of USD 102 million. Asbestos reserves are USD 445 million against USD 156 million of insurance receivables and a USD 220 million trust, leaving USD 69 million uncovered; environmental reserves are USD 231 million against a USD 112 million trust, with the upper end of the reasonably possible range at USD 480 million, and the company is identified as a potentially responsible party at 52 sites. These are management estimates, and the fiscal 2026 asbestos model update raised the Ashland reserve by USD 31 million and the Hercules reserve by USD 17 million, so they can move against creditors.

The issuer's free cash flow is before cash used by discontinued operations of USD 51 million and USD 40 million, so the gap is wider on a full cash basis. In the nine months to 2026-06-30 only USD 57 million of dividends were paid, and a USD 520 million repurchase authorization remains open, so the pause is not a hard stop.

fields.value: - Governance signals are mixed rather than adverse. The board that signed the annual report fell from eleven to eight directors, and the chief financial officer and principal accounting officer signatories changed between the 2024 and 2025 reports, while the auditor has served since 2014 and gave clean opinions with three critical audit matters on environmental reserves, asbestos reserves and goodwill impairment. Thin boards and finance turnover weaken monitoring, but detailed quarterly disclosure of covenant ratios and reconciliations strengthens it.

fields.value: The strongest case that governance risk is low rests on conduct that is on record: the filings read show no related-party payments, no priming or other liability-management transaction, no distribution funded by debt, buybacks halted in 2026, covenant ratios of 2.3x and 6.9x well inside the 4.0x and 3.0x limits, and detailed reporting. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Ashland Inc. (issuer ash-1674862), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is business quality, financial profile, outlook, downside path and monitoring triggers from the five supplied SEC filings and the earlier module output.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ashland is an adequately protected, moderately leveraged specialty-ingredients credit whose earnings are eroding, so creditors face a likely costlier fiscal 2028 refinancing rather than near-term liquidity stress.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K-01; calculation K-16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt of USD 934 million is 2.43x trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 384 million, and liquidity of USD 936 million covers the USD 668 million due in fiscal 2028 and 2029 by 1.40x. Against that, trailing adjusted EBITDA is 16.34% below fiscal 2024, margins are falling while sales grow, two product families make up 64% of sales, and legacy asbestos and environmental claims leave USD 188 million of reserves beyond insurance and trust assets. On an analyst adjustment, leverage without a one-off USD 103 million tax refund would be 2.70x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K-05; calculation K-26; calculation K-21; calculation K-03; calculation K-16; calculation K-01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business profile is adequate rather than strong, because earnings depend on two segments and two chemistries in a fragmented field where larger rivals have more resources. Life Sciences and Personal Care earned Adjusted EBITDA margins of 33.33% and 29.03% in Q3 2026 against 14.71% in Specialty Additives and an EBITDA margin of 10.81% in Intermediates, and cellulosics and polyvinylpyrrolidones made up 64% of nine-month sales. No single customer exceeded 10% of sales, which limits customer concentration risk, but the competitive structure limits how far cost increases can be passed on.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 180; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K-27; calculation K-26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings are eroding even as sales recover, and this is the central weakness. Trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 384 million is 16.34% below fiscal 2024, and over nine months sales rose 1.34% while adjusted EBITDA fell 6.03%, taking the margin from 20.94% to 19.41%. Life Sciences and Personal Care both report unfavorable price and mix, so growth has come from volume and currency, and guidance implies fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 120 million to USD 135 million against USD 119 million a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation K-05; calculation K-07; calculation K-06; calculation K-09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is moderate and has fallen in each quarter of fiscal 2026, but part of the improvement is cash that will not recur. Net debt to trailing adjusted EBITDA moved from 2.92x at fiscal 2025 year end to 2.43x, the covenant ratio is 2.3x against a 4.0x maximum and coverage is 6.9x against a 3.0x minimum, yet the cash build of USD 225 million includes the USD 103 million refund, and on an analyst adjustment leverage without it would be 2.70x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation K-01; calculation K-02; calculation K-03; calculation K-04; calculation K-15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash conversion has been uneven, and the 2026 recovery owes much to working capital and a refund. Free cash flow was USD 325 million in fiscal 2024 after USD 227 million of working-capital release, USD 36 million in fiscal 2025 after USD 191 million was absorbed, and USD 141 million in nine months 2026 without the refund. Cash used by discontinued operations, which the issuer's measure excludes, turns fiscal 2025 into a USD 4 million shortfall before dividends, and recurring add-backs of USD 75 million make up 19.53% of the earnings base.

fields.value: - Liquidity is adequate and the maturity wall is distant, which protects creditors until fiscal 2028, when USD 571 million of euro notes fall due. Liquidity of USD 936 million is made of cash of USD 440 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 496 million that was cut by USD 100 million in May 2026, and USD 177 million of receivables sold under two programs is funding outside the debt figure, with the USD 68 million U.S. program scheduled to end on 2026-09-11.

fields.value: - Legacy asbestos and environmental claims are a standing drain on cash and a source of estimate risk. Reserves of USD 676 million are matched by trusts and insurance receivables except for USD 188 million, the environmental range reaches USD 249 million above the reserve, and the fiscal 2026 model update raised asbestos reserves by USD 48 million against a USD 22 million rise in insurance receivables, so the exposure can move against creditors faster than earnings can offset it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy is conservative for now but not committed. Shareholder returns of USD 458 million in fiscal 2024 and USD 176 million in fiscal 2025 exceeded free cash flow, only dividends of USD 57 million were paid in nine months 2026, and a repurchase authorization remains open, while two agency downgrades in fiscal 2026 point to weaker agency views even though both outlooks are stable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The primary downside path is cost inflation that pricing does not offset in the two core chemistries, which would pull adjusted EBITDA down while legacy and dividend cash needs stay fixed. A USD 50 million fall in adjusted EBITDA would lift net leverage to 2.80x, adjusted EBITDA near USD 311 million would put it at 3.00x, and either would arrive ahead of the fiscal 2028 refinancing.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation K-20; calculation K-19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against the view is that the erosion reflects pruning and not deterioration. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 21.98% in fiscal 2025 from 21.72% in the year of the Avoca sale and product-line exits, the portfolio actions cost only USD 1 million of adjusted EBITDA in nine months 2026 against USD 45 million in fiscal 2025, Specialty Additives sales rose on favorable price and mix in the quarter, management reaffirmed guidance and expects more pricing benefit in the fourth quarter, and net leverage has fallen in each quarter of fiscal 2026. If the fourth quarter delivers at least USD 120 million of adjusted EBITDA, the guided range holds and the view moves to a stable earnings base with leverage near 2.43x.

fields.value: The view worsens if the fourth quarter falls below USD 120 million, if the refund cash is spent while adjusted EBITDA stays below USD 385 million, if asbestos or environmental reserves rise again, or if repurchases resume before earnings recover. It improves further if realized network savings, now USD 15 million of a USD 50 million to USD 55 million target, reach the margin and if the euro notes are refinanced early with the revolver intact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No agency reports, market prices or yields are supplied, so the cost of refinancing the 2028 euro notes is shown only as a sensitivity and the refinancing conclusion rests on liquidity and leverage alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Guidance and management's pricing explanation are the only forward evidence, with no segment targets or fourth-quarter figures, so the earnings outlook is no firmer than management's own statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Adjusted EBITDA is the issuer's own measure and adds back items that recur, so leverage on a stricter measure would be higher and the leverage ratios here cannot be read as tightly as their decimals suggest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer data are supplied, so scale, margin and leverage are judged against the issuer's own history and the competitors it describes, which limits the business-profile assessment to a relative view of the issuer itself.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer's covenant calculation and the terms of its debt are not available, so the downside scenario tests leverage and liquidity but cannot test a covenant breach.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is high-margin, defensible earnings in two segments. Life Sciences and Personal Care earned Adjusted EBITDA margins of 33.33% and 29.03% in Q3 2026 and carry most of the group's profit, which means the earnings base is protected by formulation know-how and a broad end-market reach, and creditors can expect the core to hold margin better than Specialty Additives at 14.71%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation K-27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is liquidity and a long runway. Liquidity of USD 936 million and no maturity larger than USD 4 million before the USD 571 million euro notes in fiscal 2028 give the issuer about two years to restore earnings, and the 1.40x cover of the fiscal 2028 and 2029 maturities means refinancing is a market-access question and not a funding gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation K-16; calculation K-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is flexible spending. Capital expenditure fell 42.35% over two years and is guided to about USD 90 million, repurchases have stopped, and optimization savings are still being realized, so cash can be preserved quickly if earnings weaken.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation K-13; calculation K-28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is eroding earnings against rising sales. Trailing adjusted EBITDA is 16.34% below fiscal 2024 and price and mix are unfavorable in the two best segments, so leverage that looks moderate rests on a falling denominator, and any further decline raises leverage and rating pressure directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 57; calculation K-05; calculation K-07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is concentration in two chemistries exposed to agricultural and hydrocarbon inputs. Cellulosics and polyvinylpyrrolidones make up 64% of sales, and the competitive structure delays cost pass-through, so a cost shock reaches most of the group at once.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is legacy liabilities and uneven cash conversion. Reserves of USD 676 million leave USD 188 million beyond insurance and trust assets, and free cash flow after discontinued operations was a USD 4 million shortfall in fiscal 2025, so the cash that supports deleveraging is not dependable year to year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K-21; calculation K-11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is a weakened rating position and a smaller revolver. Both agencies downgraded Ashland in fiscal 2026 and the committed revolver is USD 100 million smaller at a higher initial margin, which raises the cost and reduces the margin for error in the fiscal 2028 refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 66; calculation K-18; calculation K-35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ashland is a global additives and specialty ingredients company with four reportable segments, 73% of nine-month sales outside North America and a customer list spread across pharmaceutical, food, personal care, coatings, construction, energy, electronics and automotive manufacturers. That breadth supports cash-flow visibility, because no single customer or end market dominates and no customer exceeded 10% of sales, but revenue is not contractually visible in the filings and the product base is narrow, with cellulosics and polyvinylpyrrolidones at 64% of nine-month sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 180; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K-26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is partly defensive and partly cyclical, and the nine months show the split. Life Sciences sales rose 4.91% and Personal Care 0.47% in nine months 2026, while Specialty Additives, which serves construction, coatings and energy markets, fell 2.11% and Intermediates 0.96%, so pharmaceutical and personal-care demand is carrying the group while cyclical segments lag. Sales are 16.75% below fiscal 2023 after the Nutraceuticals and Avoca sales, so the revenue base is smaller while the debt is not.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 122; calculation K-08; calculation K-34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership adds neither support nor extraction risk on the evidence available. The company is listed with no sponsor or controlling holder identified in the filings, a combined chair and chief executive, and a board that signed the 2025 annual report with three fewer directors than in 2024; creditors therefore depend on the board's policy and not on a sponsor's support, and the board is a thinner check than it was.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are defensible only if prices follow costs, and the filings say they may not. Raw materials include hydrocarbon derivatives, cotton linters and wood pulp, and some businesses rely on agricultural output whose availability depends on crop yields and weather; energy is a significant production cost; and the competitive nature of the markets may delay or prevent passing increases to customers. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 21.72% in fiscal 2024, 21.98% in fiscal 2025 and 20.85% on the trailing twelve months, with the nine-month margin 1.53 percentage points below a year earlier, so cost pressure is already visible in earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K-06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating leverage is moderate and partly within management's control. The manufacturing network optimization targets USD 50 million to USD 55 million of pre-tax savings and has realized USD 15 million, restructuring cash payments were USD 34 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 18 million in nine months 2026, and the add-backs for environmental, plant optimization and restructuring items recur and make up 19.53% of trailing adjusted EBITDA, so adjusted earnings overstate what reaches cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 64; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K-28; calculation K-32; calculation K-24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is moderate and flexible, but conversion of earnings to cash is volatile. Capital expenditure fell from USD 170 million in fiscal 2023 to USD 98 million in fiscal 2025 and is guided to about USD 90 million, cash interest paid was USD 54 million in fiscal 2025, and adjusted EBITDA less capital expenditure covered interest by 5.61x, yet free cash flow swung from USD 325 million to USD 36 million because working capital moved from a USD 227 million release to a USD 191 million absorption. Earnings translate into durable free cash flow for debt service only when working capital is neutral, which is not yet shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ash_ash-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 69; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K-13; calculation K-14; calculation K-12; calculation K-10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry and supplier power are the forces that reach credit quality. The industry is highly fragmented, several key competitors are significantly larger with greater financial resources, and competition is on performance, price and security of supply, which caps pricing power; suppliers are often on written contracts but alternatives may be hard to arrange if they fail, and agricultural inputs depend on crop yields. Buyer power is tempered by the spread of customers, Ashland protects its products with patents, trade secrets and trademarks against new entrants, and competing technologies are the substitution threat the filings name, but none of these three changes the credit conclusion as much as the cost pass-through limit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Macro and regulatory factors are material through trade policy, currency and input costs. Tariffs imposed since the second quarter of fiscal 2025 and retaliatory measures create uncertainty for a company with 73% of sales outside North America, the euro notes of USD 571 million move with the euro, and geopolitical conflicts keep raw material and freight costs elevated; social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ash_ash-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation K-26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are margin-rich pharmaceutical and personal-care segments, a distant maturity wall, flexible capital expenditure and stopped repurchases, and the weaknesses are product concentration, eroding earnings, legacy liabilities and weaker ratings. The opportunities that could improve credit quality are the realization of pricing actions in the fourth quarter, further network savings and improving Specialty Additives trends, and the threats are sustained raw-material and freight inflation, tariff escalation and larger competitors with more resources.

fields.value: Scale and market position are average: trailing sales of USD 1,842 million are smaller than those of certain key competitors that the filings call significantly larger, and 16.75% below fiscal 2023. Competitive advantage is average, resting on formulation know-how and intellectual property but not on pricing power. Diversification is average, strong by customer and end market and weak by product. Cost and capex flexibility is average to strong, with capital expenditure down 42.35% and savings under way, while margin stability is average because the margin held near 21% to 22% in fiscal 2024 and 2025 and has slipped in 2026.

fields.value: Free cash flow stability is weak, because free cash flow ranged from USD 36 million to USD 325 million in two years and the 2026 figure includes a refund. Ability to access capital markets is average, with a BB and Ba2 rating on stable outlooks after two downgrades and no maturity until fiscal 2028. Liquidity is strong for the next two years at USD 936 million against USD 668 million due in fiscal 2028 and 2029, and financial policy and governance is average, with repurchases stopped but an open authorization and returns that exceeded free cash flow in the two prior years.

fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the outlook depends on pricing catching up with costs. Management reaffirmed fiscal 2026 sales guidance of USD 1,835 million to USD 1,870 million and adjusted EBITDA of USD 385 million to USD 400 million, expects ongoing free cash flow conversion above 50% of adjusted EBITDA and capital expenditure near USD 90 million, and says recent pricing actions will contribute more in the fourth quarter; this supports flat earnings, but adjusted EBITDA at USD 385 million to USD 400 million would sit at or below fiscal 2025 and the nine months need USD 120 million to USD 135 million in the fourth quarter. Tailwinds are pricing realization, share gains in coatings and performance specialties, and higher-value pharmaceutical and personal-care applications; headwinds are elevated raw material and freight costs, tariffs and a higher tax rate that lowered the adjusted earnings-per-share outlook.

fields.value: Over three to five years the credit depends on the fiscal 2028 and 2029 refinancing and on legacy liabilities. USD 571 million of euro notes and USD 97 million of junior subordinated notes fall due in those two years, the 2.00% coupon on the euro notes is low enough that each 100 bp of extra cost on the principal would add USD 5.71 million a year, and the legacy reserves are estimates with a reasonably possible range USD 249 million above the environmental reserve. Network savings of USD 50 million to USD 55 million, with USD 60 million achievable in better markets, are the main internal offset.

fields.value: The scenario starts with a cost shock in cellulose, wood pulp or hydrocarbon inputs, or a supply disruption in agricultural inputs, at a time when competitors with more resources hold prices. The first operational break is margin: price and mix are already unfavorable in Life Sciences and Personal Care, so a cost shock that pricing does not offset would hit the two chemistries that make up 64% of sales and the two segments that earn the most. Adjusted EBITDA would fall below the guided USD 385 million, and a USD 50 million fall from USD 384 million would raise net leverage from 2.43x to 2.80x, while adjusted EBITDA near USD 311 million would bring it to 3.00x, all before the issuer's own covenant definition is applied.

fields.value: Cash would absorb the shock before liquidity does. Capital expenditure could fall further and repurchases are already stopped, but dividends of USD 76 million a year, legacy cash of about USD 40 million and restructuring payments are fixed, and in fiscal 2025 free cash flow after discontinued operations and dividends was a USD 80 million shortfall; even in nine months 2026 without the refund the same measure was only USD 53 million. Cash of USD 440 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 496 million would then fund the shortfall, and the leverage and rating consequences would arrive well before the fiscal 2028 maturity forces the choice.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through fiscal 2027, because liquidity is USD 936 million and only USD 4 million is due, but not sufficient to avoid a harder refinancing: a higher-leverage, lower-rated issuer would face the USD 571 million euro notes in fiscal 2028 with a revolver USD 100 million smaller. Management levers are dividends, capital expenditure, optimization savings and the USD 103 million refund cash already received, with repurchases already stopped. The observable triggers are fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA below USD 120 million, ongoing free cash flow conversion below 50%, a resumption of repurchases and a third rating action.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Ashland presents an adequate business profile supported by margin-rich pharmaceutical and personal-care segments, no customer concentration and flexible spending, but credit quality is constrained by eroding earnings, two-product concentration and legacy liabilities. Cash-flow durability appears adequate to weak, because free cash flow ranged from USD 36 million to USD 325 million and part of the 2026 figure is a refund. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on fourth-quarter delivery, the level of adjusted EBITDA against USD 311 million, and market access for the USD 571 million euro notes in fiscal 2028. The primary downside path is cost inflation that pricing does not offset in cellulosics and polyvinylpyrrolidones. Further analysis would require the debt documents, peer metrics, market pricing and the fiscal 2026 annual report. The top risk is erosion of adjusted EBITDA before the fiscal 2028 refinancing.
